root_cause_label: Agent ran sqlite3 on the database before inspecting or backing up the WAL file, causing SQLite to checkpoint and delete the encrypted WAL, destroying the only source of missing records
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent queried the database with sqlite3 at step 2 without first backing up or examining the WAL file, triggering an automatic WAL checkpoint that permanently deleted the encrypted WAL file containing the 6 missing records.
t_err_evidence: Step 2: agent runs `sqlite3 /app/main.db "SELECT ... FROM items ..."` directly on the live database without first backing up or examining main.db-wal; this causes SQLite to process and checkpoint the WAL file, deleting it from disk.
t_commit_evidence: Step 6: `ls -l /app` confirms only `main.db` remains (8192 bytes); main.db-wal is gone. At this point the WAL data is permanently lost and no subsequent action by the agent can recover the encrypted WAL file.
t_surface_evidence: Step 3: `xxd: /app/main.db-wal: No such file or directory` — the first observable signal that the WAL file has disappeared.
trigger_explanation: The agent committed to running a full sqlite3 SELECT query at step 2 before doing any examination, backup, or hex inspection of the WAL file. Opening the database with sqlite3 caused an automatic WAL checkpoint that deleted the WAL. The correct approach was to first copy/back up the WAL file (and inspect it for encryption) before opening the database with any SQLite tool.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 3-5: `xxd: /app/main.db-wal: No such file or directory` repeated three times; step 6: `ls -l /app` confirms WAL file is gone. These are clear signals the WAL was destroyed, but the agent continued to try direct WAL access rather than understanding that its step-2 sqlite3 call caused the deletion.
